// diagnostic

E0446

`+` needs two arrays of one length, but these are `[Int#3]` and `[Int#4]`

What

`+` needs two arrays of one length, but these are `[Int#3]` and `[Int#4]`

Why

An operator on two fixed arrays pairs each slot of one with the same slot of the other, so every slot needs a partner

Fix

Make both arrays the same length, or take a slice of the longer one

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0446: Tests/UI/fixed_array_elementwise_mismatch.stderr.

Error [jet.FixedArrayElementwiseMismatch]: `+` needs two arrays of one length, but these are `[Int#3]` and `[Int#4]`
  --> Tests/UI/fixed_array_elementwise_mismatch.jet:9:11
    |
  9 |     print(three + four)
    |           ^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: An operator on two fixed arrays pairs each slot of one with the same slot of the other, so every slot needs a partner
 Fix: Make both arrays the same length, or take a slice of the longer one

Error [jet.FixedArrayElementwiseMismatch]: `*` needs two arrays of one element type, but these are `[Int#3]` and `[Float#3]`
  --> Tests/UI/fixed_array_elementwise_mismatch.jet:10:11
    |
 10 |     print(three * floats)
    |           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: Each slot is the scalar `*` on two elements, and that needs one number type on both sides
 Fix: Convert one array's elements to the other's type first
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0446

Error [jet.FixedArrayElementwiseMismatch]: `*` combines `[Int#3]` with another `[Int#3]` or with one `Int`, but this is `Float`
  --> Tests/UI/fixed_array_elementwise_mismatch.jet:11:11
    |
 11 |     print(three * scale)
    |           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: A value beside a fixed array is applied to every slot, so it needs the slots' type
 Fix: Convert the value to `Int`, or make it an array of the same shape
